papers.relied_on: Abstract-level case report taken as support that a calcium-stimulated insulin gradient chooses which pancreatic territory to resect when imaging is negative (row 22 D1, D2, D3, D7) and as an example of a procedure with notable burden (D6).
papers.full_text_shows: One 37-year-old woman with Whipple's triad, fasting glucose 31 mg/dl with IRI 11.6 uU/mL, negative CT, MRI and EUS; the selective arterial calcium injection (SACI) test showed a step-up only in the gastroduodenal artery, twice (before and after octreotide), and pancreatoduodenectomy relieved symptoms for about 1 year, after which symptoms recurred and a remnant total pancreatectomy was needed. No pre-operative SACI result for the remnant is given, and histology did not fully meet nesidioblastosis criteria (no islet increase; many isolated insulin-producing cells). No SACI complications are reported or discussed; the paper is silent on the burden of the test.
papers.quote: blood vessels with plasma insulin levels that were more than double the basal level after calcium injection were considered positive
papers.key_numbers: Fasting PG 31 mg/dl, IRI 11.6 uU/mL, CPR 6.6 ng/mL; 12-h fast PG 45 mg/dl, IRI 10.0 uU/mL; SACI dose 0.025 mEq/kg calcium gluconate, positive if insulin more than double basal; step-up only in GDA; Japan survey 2017-2018: 205 insulinoma vs 9 adult nesidioblastosis cases (cited in the paper).
papers.role_in_work: Case-report support (single case) for row 22 beyond ENETS 2016; not independent evidence of decision impact.
papers.design: Single case report with 5+ year follow-up (died of sepsis at 7 years, unrelated).
papers.population_and_size: n=1, adult woman, clinically diagnosed adult-onset nesidioblastosis, negative imaging, no MEN1, no diabetes.
papers.measure_type: Stimulated insulin (selective arterial calcium injection with hepatic-vein insulin sampling); also fasting-test insulin, C-peptide and an octreotide loading test (insulin and glucose).
papers.assay_or_platform: Immunoreactive insulin (IRI) and C-peptide immunoreactivity (CPR), platform not named; units uU/mL and ng/mL.
papers.quality_note: Case report; diagnosis made clinically, histology only partly met criteria; recurrence in the remnant means the head-only gradient did not predict the whole disease; no conflicts section checked in the extract.

papers.relied_on: Row 48 reasons describe it as a single-centre study of 69 adults with obesity in which the diagnosis rests on glucose and symptoms, insulin collected but not used as a criterion, no insulin threshold.
papers.full_text_shows: The 69 participants were healthy volunteers with obesity, without diabetes and with a 2-h OGTT glucose of 155 mg/dL or less, not patients referred for hypoglycaemia. Reactive hypoglycaemia (RH) was defined from the MMTT glucose curve only (decline rate and early nadir, or absolute minimum 78 mg/dL or less within 80 min), with the cut-off taken from the cohort's own median decline; the authors state symptoms were not recorded. Insulin entered only through an IVGTT (sensitivity, disposition index), not through the meal-test definition, and the RH group had higher insulin sensitivity and no higher acute insulin response.
papers.quote: RH symptoms were not recorded in the postprandial period of the MMTT
papers.key_numbers: N=69: 51 non-RH, 18 RH in Results (limitations say 19 observations); RH criteria: post-peak decline <= -1.2 mg/dL/min with early nadir >= 5 mg/dL below fasting, or minimum <= 78 mg/dL within 80 min; MMTT 7 kcal/kg, blood to 240 min; IVGTT: greater SI and DI in RH, no difference in AIRg or insulin clearance (p=0.1); the paper says validation in a larger sample is needed before the criteria can be implemented.
papers.role_in_work: Supporting source for the row 48 research-only status (a research definition of reactive hypoglycaemia); not a diagnostic accuracy study.
papers.design: Cross-sectional physiology study (MMTT plus IVGTT within 7 days), single centre (University of Alabama at Birmingham), with a logistic-regression model on a down-sampled data set.
papers.population_and_size: 69 healthy, non-diabetic adults aged 21-50 with obesity (African American and Caucasian American); RH group 18 (19 in the limitations text).
papers.measure_type: Post-meal (4-h liquid mixed-meal test) glucose and insulin, and IV-glucose (IVGTT) insulin with C-peptide measured; RH defined by glucose alone.
papers.assay_or_platform: Glucose oxidase (Stanbio Sirrus); insulin by TOSOH AIA-II immunofluorescence (inter-assay CV 4.42%); C-peptide by double-antibody radioimmunoassay; MINMOD for SI.
papers.quality_note: Small, non-patient sample; the definition is circular (cut-off from the cohort median, then used to define groups); no symptoms, no counter-regulatory hormones; down-sampling for the model; no conflict statement found in the extracted text.

papers.relied_on: Case report taken as support for the calcium-stimulated insulin gradient in insulinoma localisation (row 22 D1, D2, D3, D7) and for procedure burden (D6).
papers.full_text_shows: A 53-year-old man had a 10 mm hypervascular pancreatic-head tumour on CT and EUS, so imaging was not negative. Exendin-4 PET/CT and PET/MRI localised the tumour; SACST was done afterwards, was positive only for the superior mesenteric artery territory (insulin 31 to 240.1 uU/mL at 40 s) and negative for the gastroduodenal artery, and the authors say SACST 'supported functional localization'. The paper's main message is a non-invasive alternative; it cites a phase II trial in which exendin PET found 100% of insulinomas against SACST 89% (second-hand). A 75 g OGTT with insulin and C-peptide to 300 min was also done (glucose 55 mg/dL with IRI 17.2 uU/mL at 300 min) but did not drive a decision because fasting hypoglycaemia was already documented.
papers.quote: SACST subsequently demonstrated a positive response from the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) territory
papers.key_numbers: ED glucose 27 mg/dL with IRI 40.5 uU/mL; OGTT 300 min glucose 55 mg/dL, IRI 17.2 uU/mL, C-peptide 2.18 ng/mL; SACST SMA insulin 31 to 240.1 uU/mL; tumour 13 x 10 mm; PET SUVmax 15.4 (PET/CT) and 22.5 (PET/MRI) vs background 4.87 and 3.33; cited comparators (from reference 23): CT 83%, MRI 63%, EUS 90%, SACST 89%, exendin PET 100%; 24 months without recurrence.
papers.role_in_work: Case-report citation for row 22; in fact a case for a non-invasive competitor to the stimulated-insulin gradient, with SACST as an adjunct.
papers.design: Single case report with a short literature review of PET/MRI.
papers.population_and_size: n=1, adult man with a solitary pancreatic-head insulinoma (not MEN1, not negative imaging).
papers.measure_type: Stimulated insulin (selective arterial calcium stimulation test, hepatic-vein insulin); post-load (75 g OGTT) insulin and C-peptide; random insulin during hypoglycaemia.
papers.assay_or_platform: Immunoreactive insulin (IRI) and C-peptide, platform not named.
papers.quality_note: Case report; SACST done after localisation, so it cannot show decision impact; the territory it picked (SMA) differs from the tumour's head location on cross-sectional imaging, which the authors explain by SMA arterial supply on CT angiography; the 89% and 100% figures are second-hand from the paper's reference list.

papers.relied_on: Abstract read as a case-level source showing suppressed insulin and C-peptide steering to IGF-II testing in non-islet cell tumour hypoglycaemia (row 21 D2 = 1).
papers.full_text_shows: An eight-case treatment series from one UK reference laboratory. Insulin and C-peptide are reported in the tables (below 10 pmol/l and below 100 pmol/l during hypoglycaemia in the cases tabulated) and as markers of recovery of secretion on glucocorticoid treatment, but the paper states that the principal diagnostic parameter is the IGF ratio, and the question studied is treatment effectiveness, not the diagnostic use of insulin or C-peptide.
papers.quote: The principal diagnostic parameter is the IGF ratio, calculated from total IGF-II /IGF-I.
papers.key_numbers: 8 cases; more than 120 NICTH cases diagnosed in the laboratory since 1990; IGF ratio normally below 10; Case 1 day 1: glucose 1.8 mmol/l, insulin <10 pmol/l, C-peptide <100 pmol/l, IGF ratio 40.1; Case 6: insulin and C-peptide undetectable during hypoglycaemia while sulfonylurea ingestion had first been suspected.
papers.role_in_work: Case-series support for row 21 (NICTH); evidence level 1 for the insulin/C-peptide branch.
papers.design: Retrospective case series of referred patients with serial samples.
papers.population_and_size: 8 adults with NICTH (lung, sarcoma, fibroma, prostate and other tumours).
papers.measure_type: Random (during hypoglycaemia) insulin and C-peptide, plus IGF-I and IGF-II; not post-meal or stimulated.
papers.assay_or_platform: Mercodia ELISA for insulin and C-peptide; in-house IGF-II and big IGF-II assays; Nichols Advantage IGF-I.
papers.quality_note: Eight referred cases, uncontrolled, treatment-response focus; PDF-derived text (some symbol loss, decimal points garbled) but readable.

papers.relied_on: Context only for row 3 D7: 97,648 insulin-related hypoglycaemia ED visits a year, with sulfonylurea use documented in 39.2% of those with an oral agent.
papers.full_text_shows: The study counts insulin-related hypoglycaemia events in insulin-treated patients; sulfonylureas appear only as concomitant agents among insulin users. It contains no estimate of sulfonylurea-only hypoglycaemia and no insulin, C-peptide or drug-screen testing data, so it cannot size the sulfonylurea-ingestion branch of row 3. Confirms the context-only use.
papers.quote: Metformin and sulfonylureas were the most commonly-documented concomitant oral diabetes agents
papers.key_numbers: 97,648 ED visits a year (CI 64,410-130,887), 2007-2011; about 30,000 hospitalisations a year; 9.2% of ED visits for all adverse drug events; sulfonylureas 39.2% (CI 34.8-43.6) of visits where an oral agent was documented; an oral agent was documented in 17.1% of adult visits.
papers.role_in_work: Contextual denominator source for the row 3 D7 chain; not used in the arithmetic.
papers.design: National surveillance estimate (NEISS-CADES) combined with NHIS survey denominators.
papers.population_and_size: 8,100 surveillance cases, weighted to national estimates, 2007-2011, US.
papers.measure_type: None (no insulin or C-peptide test); relevant only as event frequency.
papers.assay_or_platform: Not applicable (medical-record abstraction of hypoglycaemia events).
papers.quality_note: Surveillance data; underestimates hypoglycaemia cared for outside the ED; insulin-treated denominator comes from a separate survey.

papers.relied_on: No score entry cites it; it appears only in the V7 search log (row 13 D7 search, 'abnormal glucose metabolism after TIA or minor stroke') and in corpus.csv as V7: text.
papers.full_text_shows: A CHANCE trial subanalysis in Chinese patients with minor stroke or TIA, which used only fasting plasma glucose (impaired fasting glucose and diabetes versus normal); no insulin, C-peptide, HOMA-IR or OGTT was measured, and the authors list the absence of OGTT-based IGT and HbA1c as a limitation. It therefore says nothing about insulin-based measurement.
papers.quote: Both IFG and DM were associated with an increased risk of stroke in patients with a minor stroke or TIA.
papers.role_in_work: Search-log item only; could serve as a side check of the share without diabetes after minor stroke or TIA (about 69%, Chinese, admission glucose), but is not used in any score or claim.
papers.design: Post hoc analysis of a randomised trial (CHANCE, clopidogrel plus aspirin vs aspirin).
papers.population_and_size: 5,135 Chinese adults aged 40 or older with minor ischemic stroke or high-risk TIA.
papers.measure_type: Non-insulin surrogate (fasting plasma glucose only); no insulin or C-peptide.
papers.assay_or_platform: Fasting plasma glucose within 2 days of admission; local hospital laboratories.
papers.quality_note: Good for what it measures; population not US; only single fasting glucose, so undiagnosed prediabetes and diabetes are misclassified.

papers.relied_on: Row 13 V7 D7 uses 29.6% with diabetes (patients aged 65 or older) to set the share without diabetes at 70% (range 65-80%).
papers.full_text_shows: 29.6% had diabetes among 409,060 ischaemic stroke survivors aged 65 or older, using a definition of prior history or a new clinical diagnosis in hospital; an alternative definition adding medication use gave 32.3%. The authors say they probably missed patients with undiagnosed diabetes, the cohort excludes in-hospital deaths and patients under 65, and the registry holds no insulin or glucose-challenge data. The 70% share therefore holds for older survivors with a lower bound nearer 65-68%, within the stated range of 65-80%.
papers.quote: Third, we probably missed patients without a prior diagnosis of diabetes
papers.key_numbers: 409,060 patients; diabetes 29.6% (n=120,989); alternative definition 32.3% (n=132,220); only 48.3% of diabetic patients had HbA1c data; 3-year mortality 46.0% vs 44.2%.
papers.role_in_work: Source of the share without diabetes in the row 13 D7 patient chain (an assumption-bearing step).
papers.design: Registry cohort linked to Medicare claims, 2003-2011, 3-year follow-up.
papers.population_and_size: 409,060 US patients aged 65 or older with ischaemic stroke, 1,690 hospitals.
papers.measure_type: None for insulin; diabetes status from history or clinical diagnosis (non-insulin surrogate).
papers.assay_or_platform: Registry abstraction and claims; HbA1c only partly available.
papers.quality_note: Large, US, but older patients only and diabetes classification relies on diagnosis; author conflict statements present (a general disclosure list), none specific to this use.

proposals.reason: Neither case report is guideline text; no change.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 48 (Sweatt 2026 entry) and V21/V23/V24 reasons
claim_issues.issue: The row says the counts '69 adults, 19 meeting it' come from the abstract. The full text gives 51 non-RH and 18 RH in the Results (19 in the limitations paragraph), so the RH count is 18 or 19. The row does not say the 69 are healthy non-diabetic volunteers with obesity (not patients), that symptoms were not recorded, that the cut-off (-1.2 mg/dL/min) was taken from the cohort's own median, or that the definition has a second route (minimum 78 mg/dL or less within 80 min). V21 also says the two studies 'rest the diagnosis on glucose and symptoms'; for this paper there were no symptoms.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Sweatt 2026 (PMID 41829992, DOI 10.3390/nu18050822), full text: 69 healthy non-diabetic adults with obesity (18 classified as reactive hypoglycaemia in the Results, 19 in the limitations text) had a 4-h mixed-meal test and an IVGTT; reactive hypoglycaemia was defined from the meal-test glucose curve alone (decline <= -1.2 mg/dL/min with an early nadir >= 5 mg/dL below fasting, or a minimum <= 78 mg/dL within 80 min), the rate taken from the cohort median; symptoms were not recorded and the authors call for validation before use.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 48, insulin remark on Sweatt 2026
claim_issues.issue: The row says the insulin phenotypes come from an IVGTT, not the meal test. This is right, but the conclusion drawn in the paper is also that reactive hypoglycaemia was linked with greater insulin sensitivity and disposition index and not with higher acute insulin response or exaggerated insulin secretion, which is worth stating because it argues against reading a high post-meal insulin as the criterion.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: In the IVGTT the reactive-hypoglycaemia group had higher insulin sensitivity and disposition index, with no difference in acute insulin response or insulin clearance; the authors write that it is 'not by overall insulin hypersecretion'.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 22 and claims UC-22 ('Case reports PMIDs 40656591, 41833398, abstracts')
claim_issues.issue: The read level is now full text. The two cases do not both fit the row's population: PMID 41833398 is a solitary pancreatic-head insulinoma with positive CT and EUS (not negative imaging, not MEN1), localised by exendin-4 PET, with SACST done afterwards; it is better described as a non-invasive competitor. PMID 40656591 is a negative-imaging adult nesidioblastosis case with a head-only step-up in the gastroduodenal artery, but disease recurred in the remnant after a head resection.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Case reports, full text: PMID 40656591 (DOI 10.2147/ceg.s520986), one negative-imaging case of adult-onset nesidioblastosis with a gastroduodenal-artery-only calcium step-up, relief for about a year after pancreatoduodenectomy, then remnant recurrence requiring total pancreatectomy; PMID 41833398 (DOI 10.1507/endocrj.ej25-0591), one imaging-positive pancreatic-head insulinoma where SACST (superior mesenteric territory) was an adjunct after exendin-4 PET localisation; neither case measures decision impact.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 21 (Teale 2004, PMID 15049960 is cited as a source in V15 D2 only)
claim_issues.issue: Not an issue in the row text, which does not cite the paper; if cited, note that insulin and C-peptide are reported as undetectable or below assay limits during hypoglycaemia in a treatment series and the paper itself calls the IGF ratio the principal diagnostic parameter.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Teale 2004 (PMID 15049960, DOI 10.1111/j.1365-2265.2004.01989.x), full text: eight NICTH cases; insulin below 10 pmol/l and C-peptide below 100 pmol/l during hypoglycaemia in the tabulated cases; the IGF-II to IGF-I ratio is the principal diagnostic parameter; treatment (glucocorticoid, surgery) is the main question studied.

notes: Read only local files, no web. Path to viability: row 22 may be affected in one way, not as a score change: C130 shows a non-invasive exendin-4 PET/MRI route (and cites a phase II trial with PET 100% against SACST 89%, second-hand and not checked), so the stimulated-insulin gradient may become a niche test for exendin-negative or discordant cases; the paper itself says systematic studies are needed. Row 48 path to viability is unchanged (needs a validated glucose-plus-insulin criterion in symptomatic patients; C129 states validation in a larger sample is needed). C222 has no insulin measure and no claim cites it (grep of claims.csv, usecases-verified.md, merged-conclusion.md found nothing), so proposals are null and no claim issue is raised. Rubric clarification 17 (D6 as the lower of burden and false-result consequence) cannot be checked against the case reports because they say nothing about SACI harm. Current scores were taken from S4.json, S3.json, V12.json, V15.json, V1.json, V7.json, V21.json, V23.json and V24.json; V7 supersedes U1 for D7. A null proposed value is used to mean no change. Conflict statements: C228 lists author disclosures (general); none were found in the extracted text of C129, C122 or C130 beyond what is stated in the quality notes. About 31 tool calls used.
